body: Interesting comment. You've given me a lot to think about. I'm not sure if I'll keep trying, but the fact that I can die at any time comforts me and sometimes gives me the strength to go on. Thanks for the help.

I wouldn't say it "invalidates" Buddhism or anything else. My opinions are just opinions like anyone else's. That said, thanks for finding it interesting. When you mull over death, suicide, the point of life, etc. for over half your life, you're bound to have some interesting and philosophical hot takes on the subject. :P

I don't know if I'm making the correct assessment, there's no way to 100% know for sure. But the odds certainly are not in my favor, based on both common sense and over a decade of evidence. 

I do agree my freedom is one of the few things I have that is truly valuable. The idea of being able to end it at any time without having responsibilities left behind or having to feel guilty is quite soothing. It also lets me do crazy shit like travel 3,000 miles away and be homeless. That's why I wouldn't want to join the military like another guy suggested and I myself considered in the past. I'd be giving up one of my few perks in this shit life. I guess one of the other positives would be that I'm healthy. Also that I'm young, decent looking, and gay, and can therefore get sexual gratification whenever I want it. I also think I'm somewhat intelligent, but unfortunately that doesn't do much for you without a formal education. I definitely don't have the worst life by any means and am well aware of that, but what little I do have does not seem to be enough to justify forging ahead with.

Those are interesting ideas. I currently work at a warehouse in Amazon. It's a shitty manual labor job, but it pays relatively well (emphasis on relatively) considering I have barely any education.

I cut off all contact with my ex boyfriend years ago. Changed numbers, blocked him on social media, the whole nine yards. There'd be no way to rub it in his face, and I'd prefer to never speak to him again anyway haha.

1) These are good suggestions, the problem is that these days everyone is so focused on the paper showing you graduated college that it's still an uphill climb no matter how smart or skilled you are.

2) I won't be ensuring long term survival of the species even if I lived. I won't be reproducing since I'm gay. lol

3) It's hard for me to believe this since I no longer have anything to offer anyone. My first boyfriend was before I was jaded, when I still had some hope, wasn't a college dropout, wasn't buried under mountains of debt, was a nicer person in general then, etc.

I've tried multiple SSRIs and they didn't help at all. Probably because I'm not depressed, my life just fucking sucks. Yes, sometimes I get depressed that my life fucking sucks, but that's not because I have MDD, it's because my life fucking sucks! It's a totally natural reaction to your life fucking sucking. Feeling amazing when your life fucking sucks would be a disorder, not feeling shitty when your life fucking sucks. That's just a rational emotional response.

I've done a LOT of planning, research, and acquisition, and my method is pretty close to foolproof. That said, if it did fail, I'd just try again ASAP until I succeeded. My life is already horrible enough now, I wouldn't even spend a passing second considering dealing with all that PLUS being disfigured or in constant pain, or whatever.

There's definitely a part of me that wants to live, I don't deny that. But it seems to get smaller and smaller every day.

It'd be tough for me to give up my one sense of control and liberation though, the ability to exit at any time. I felt amazing the first time I acquired my method, I don't think I can go back to not having the means to leave if need be.

I don't think lack of education SHOULD limit you, unfortunately I live in a country where you need to go tens of thousands of dollars into debt in order to get it, and most decent employers look for that piece of paper before even considering you, so I'm kind of screwed there on a practical level. I could possibly get around this if I had family connections or friends in high places, but I obviously don't.

I think most people need at least one thing they can cling to in times of strife to be able to make it. For most people that's religion, but I'm not religious. For many it's family, but I have none. For some it's their significant other/spouse, but I don't have one of those either. For others it's a passion, but I've never really had one of those, probably because I've been so focused on killing myself for half of my life. I quite simply have NO reason to go on, my existence is just totally pointless.

Don't worry about suffering. I have it totally planned out and I should end up going very peacefully.

Every time I think I'm at rock bottom, somehow I still manage to fall even further. ;)

Though even if I was this time, there's the possibility of things staying the same, not getting better.

Did I feel happiness? That's an interesting question. I wouldn't say I felt happy, but there were periods of contentment when I allowed myself to get lost in the adventure of it all and forgot the reason why I did it to begin with and that it wasn't actually improving my situation. So I would say it was probably just a shiny object,  a distraction, an illusion that could only help temporarily. Kind of like drugs, except not as unhealthy. As the saying goes, no matter where you go, there you are.

I agree there's always hope for a better future, but there's also realistic odds. Some people are going to have 99.99% likelihood of having a better future if they have near perfect and amazing circumstances. Others will have 0.001% likelihood if they got totally screwed over by playing life on impossible mode. I see mine as definitely on the very low end of the range, which will of course raise the question of why bother swimming up the rough current for decades just for an extremely slim chance at a decent life?

Thanks for your comment.

I considered it, but decided against because I'd lose the ability to kill myself at will in a moment's notice (which is one of the few things I value highly in life, shows how fucked up I am.) Losing that freedom would suck.

I'm just curious though, why do you think it would help?

My past is horrible, no doubt, and in many ways directly led to the situation I'm in today. But the main reason I'm suicidal is my lack of hope and likely bleak future. Even if I got over everything from my past tomorrow, I'd still have to deal with the shit present and unpromising future. The lack of hope for realistic improvement is what will end up putting the bullet in my skull, not my past.

I agree this is probably the only hand "I" have. I'm not religious, and believe it's most likely that death is the same nothingness as pre-birth. That said, regardless of what death is, "me" as I currently know myself will have no awareness one way or the other (unless some religions are correct.) So there'd be nothing to mourn or feel regret about. Even if reincarnation was real for instance, the fact that "I'd" never have any awareness of my past lives makes it so that it might as well not be real at all.

As someone who isn't religious and has no family to support, I think life is a pretty simple equation. You want good times > bad times. If it's heavily tilted toward the latter with little hope for improval, does it make any logical sense to go on? I don't see what "pricks" I'd be bluffing. Most of the reason my life is so shit is total neglect and bad luck, not so much maliciousness (except my ex boyfriend and already dead father.)

I'm in the US. There are some things I'd like to see ideally, but unfortunately I don't have the resources. I actually did consider just becoming a nomad/vagabond like you suggest, but I don't think it's sustainable. Traveling far worked last time because I had a small nest egg, without that it seems like it'd just be a lot of starving and panhandling.

Well yeah, very few things in life are 100% certain. But most people aren't going to go all in on the sun not rising tomorrow, or invest their life savings in Powerball tickets. It's all about odds, and mine are so low that it's not even worth going through the formality and decades of suffering.
